harmonicFunction: E (I) - Stark, percussive major/power-chord anchor in the verse
Em (i) - Parallel minor tonic unleashing urgency in the chorus
C (bVI) - Submediant lift adding breadth to the chorus
G (bIII) - Relative major warmth contrasting with the E minor plea
D (bVII) - Subtonic stepping stone leading toward the turnaround
B (V) - Secondary/harmonic minor dominant resolving with maximum tension back to Em

techniques.name: Syncopated Staccato Rock Strumming & Choked Stabs
techniques.description: Punchy, militant rhythm guitar work combining palm-muted verse hits with wide-open acoustic and electric chorus strumming

sequence: Lock in with the bass riff during the verse using tight, muted E5, G, and A hits
Drive the pre-chorus with steady eighth-note downstrokes on A and G
Open up your strumming hand for wide, ringing Em - C - G chords in the chorus
Punch the D to B turnaround chords with decisive rhythmic authority
tips: In the verse, use your fretting hand and palm to choke the strings immediately after the G and A stabs
Beginners can substitute open B7 (X-2-1-2-0-2) for the B major barre chord at the end of the chorus
Keep the 125 BPM march groove rock-steady without rushing the syncopated rests
details.progression: Em - C - G - Em - C - D - B

techniques.name: Martin Rotsey & Jim Moginie Angular Horn-Doubling & Leading Tones
techniques.description: Biting single-coil lead phrasing doubling the iconic horn fanfare, combined with sharp octave punches and the dramatic D# leading tone over the dominant B major turnaround

notes: High horn melody: 12th fret high E -> 10th fret -> 7th fret -> 8th fret B
Leading tone: D# at 4th fret G string (or 1st fret D string) resolving upward to E
Sharp percussive pick attack on Stratocaster bridge/middle pickup
sequence: Punch the brass-line melody in tight unison with Rob Hirst's snare accents
Sustain the high notes with crisp, rapid finger vibrato
Dig in hard on the B major turnaround to emphasize the dramatic tension
tips: Use a Stratocaster in the middle or bridge pickup position with slight compression
Keep pick strokes short, precise, and detached (staccato) to match brass articulation
Do not allow open strings to bleed over the sharp rhythmic rests

sections.name: Intro Bass Riff & Staccato Guitar Punches
sections.technique: Syncopated Staccato Rock Strumming & Choked Stabs
sections.description: Peter Gifford's iconic pulsing bassline answered by sharp, syncopated E, G, and A power chord punches.
notes: Leave dynamic space and silence during the initial bass pedal
Snap sharply into the G5 and A5 hits with immediate fret-hand muting
Let the silence breathe between the hits

sections.name: Verse 1 Outback Storytelling & Choked Hits
sections.technique: Syncopated Staccato Rock Strumming & Choked Stabs
sections.description: Peter Garrett delivers the urgent environmental narrative ('Out where the river broke...') over sparse, rhythmic guitar chugs.
notes: Keep the rhythm taut and dry with palm muting
Strike the G and A chords on the upbeats of beats 2 and 4
Leave maximum headroom for the vocal delivery

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Eighth-Note March ('The Time Has Come')
sections.description: The rhythm section locks into relentless eighth-note downstrokes on A and G, marching with increasing tension toward the chorus.
notes: Drive the tempo with steady eighth-note downstrokes at 125 BPM
Crescendo gradually over the four measures
Prepare for the explosive dynamic burst into the chorus

sections.name: Chorus Explosion ('How Can We Dance')
sections.description: The song explodes into full stadium power on 'How can we dance when our earth is turning?', resolving through Em, C, G, D, and B.
sections.progression: Em - C - G - Em - C - D - B
notes: Unleash full-arm strums across all six strings on Em and G
Clean change into the C major cowboy chord
Hit the dominant B major barre chord with decisive tension on beat 3

sections.name: Horn Section Doubling & Lead Guitar Break
sections.technique: Martin Rotsey & Jim Moginie Angular Horn-Doubling & Leading Tones
sections.description: Martin Rotsey and Jim Moginie double the iconic brass fanfare riff with biting Stratocaster single-coil cut, weaving punchy octaves and resolving on the dramatic D# leading tone of the B major chord.
notes: Play the horn melody cleanly at the 12th and 10th frets of the high E string
Keep note attacks detached and punchy like brass stabs
Hit the D# leading tone on the 4th fret G string to outline the major V chord B
Sustain into the crashing return of the chorus

sections.name: Final Stadium Chorus & Marching Outro
sections.description: Maximum stadium energy as the horns, guitars, and Garrett's impassioned vocals chant the chorus, culminating in sudden dramatic halts.
sections.progression: Em - C - G - D - B (repeating to sudden stop)
notes: Maintain fierce 125 BPM downstroke intensity
Accentuate the high 12th and 15th fret lead fills
Stop dead on the final B chord hit with absolute silence

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul Junior / Fender Telecaster (Jim Moginie & Martin Rotsey) plus Acoustic Dreadnought
guitar.pickup: Bridge P-90 or single-coil pickup with bright, cutting attack

settings.bass: 5 (tight low end leaving room for bass riff)

effects.reverb: Large hall reverb on brass and chorus guitars
effects.other: Chorus pedal (subtle) on clean electric layers

beginner.title: Chorus Open Chords & B7 Option
steps: Practice the Em - C - G chorus movement at 100 BPM
Learn the D to B7 (X-2-1-2-0-2) turnaround at the end of the chorus
Play the A to G pre-chorus with steady downstrokes
Combine verse stabs, pre-chorus, and chorus at 125 BPM

intermediate.title: Full B Barre Chord & Tight Verse Muting
steps: Replace B7 with the full A-shape B major barre chord (X-2-4-4-4-2)
Lock your right-hand palm muting into the syncopated verse G and A hits
Add the acoustic 16th-note strumming layer during the chorus

advanced.title: Dual-Guitar Interplay & Brass Voicings
steps: Arrange both Jim Moginie and Martin Rotsey's interlocking guitar parts
Transcribe the horn-section counter-melodies onto upper-register triads
Perform at 125 BPM with relentless dynamic control

commonMistakes: Staying on E major instead of switching to E minor when the chorus begins
Letting the verse chords ring too long instead of muting tightly with the bass
Missing the switch from G to D-B on the second half of the chorus
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: Em → C → G quick-change drill (2 beats each on Em and C, 4 beats on G)
4 minutes: C → D → B turnaround transition practice
4 minutes: Verse E - G - A syncopated stabs with metronome at 125 BPM
focusAreas: Harmonic contrast between the E major verse and E minor chorus
Clean D to B major turnaround
metronomeWork: Start at 100 BPM to master the fast Em-C-G changes
Increase to 115 BPM while integrating the B major barre chord
Play at album tempo of 125 BPM with crisp staccato muting in the verses
